223	      return
224	    }
225	  }
226	
227	  // stuck detection escalation ladder (user law 2026-09-01 v2: RCON tp
228	  // RETIRED — bots self-rescue LEGIT): 1st detection = stop + relog; still
229	  // frozen at the SAME spot on a later detection = send the bot's own
230	  // `/trigger home` chat command (cavehome datapack — works only if the bot
231	  // ran `/trigger sethome` on the surface first, which is fleet doctrine).
232	  // No home set / trigger fails = nothing more the overseer may do: log loud
233	  // and leave it for the orchestrator's stuck report.
234	  if (running && st.pos) {
235	    const key = `${Math.round(st.pos.x)},${Math.round(st.pos.y)},${Math.round(st.pos.z)}`
236	    if (s.lastPos === key) {
237	      if (now - s.posSince > STUCK_MS && st.currentTask.kind === 'goto') {
238	        if (s.stuckAtKey === key) {
239	          log(`${bot.name} STILL stuck at ${key} after relog -> last-resort /trigger home (no tp — retired)`)
240	          await api(bot.port, '/stop', {})
241	          await api(bot.port, '/chat', { message: '/trigger home' })
242	          await grey(bot.name, bot.color, '(overseer) hard-stuck — sent /trigger home (works only if sethome done)')
243	          s.stuckAtKey = null
244	        } else {
245	          log(`${bot.name} stuck at ${key} -> stop + relog (tp next if still frozen)`)
246	          await api(bot.port, '/stop', {})
247	          await api(bot.port, '/relog', {})
248	          await grey(bot.name, bot.color, '(overseer) stuck — relogged; /trigger home next if still frozen')
249	          s.stuckAtKey = key
250	        }
251	        s.posSince = now
252	      }
253	    } else { s.lastPos = key; s.posSince = now; s.stuckAtKey = null }
254	    s.idleSince = null
255	    return
256	  }
257	
258	  // recurring chores: due + bot free → fire (before idle-defaults, higher value)
259	  for (const ch of CHORES) {
260	    if (ch.bot !== bot.name) continue
261	    const last = choreLast.get(ch.id) ?? (ch.offsetMs ? now - ch.everyMs + ch.offsetMs : 0)
262	    if (now - last < ch.everyMs) continue
263	    choreLast.set(ch.id, now)
264	    const r = await api(bot.port, ch.ep, ch.body)
265	    if (r && !r.error) {
266	      log(`${bot.name} chore ${ch.id} -> ${ch.ep}`)
267	      await grey(bot.name, bot.color, `(overseer) ${ch.say}`)
268	      s.idleSince = null
269	      return
270	    }
271	  }
272	
273	  // idle tracking — RE-ENABLED 2026-09-01 with safe per-role defaults (see the
274	  // header block). Reachable only when nothing is running: the running-task
275	  // branch above returns before this point, so a default can never land on a
276	  // busy bot.
277	  const IDLE_DEFAULTS_ENABLED = true
278	  if (!IDLE_DEFAULTS_ENABLED) return
279	  if (s.idleSince == null) { s.idleSince = now; return }
280	  if (now - s.idleSince < IDLE_MS) return
281	
282	  // idle past threshold → role-default task. NEVER `force` — one commander:
283	  // the overseer fills dead air, it does not cancel a driver's work. If the
284	  // runner answers busy, that is the correct outcome; log it and move on.
285	  // A rotation entry is either a static {ep, body, say} or a chooser function
286	  // (status) => {ep, body, say} that picks based on live bot state. A chooser
287	  // may return null/undefined to mean "nothing useful right now" — skip quietly.
288	  const slot = bot.defaults[s.defaultIdx % bot.defaults.length]
289	  s.defaultIdx++
290	  s.idleSince = null
291	  const d = typeof slot === 'function' ? slot(st) : slot
292	  if (!d) return

294	  if (res && res.ok !== false && !res.error) {
295	    log(`${bot.name} idle>${IDLE_MS / 1000}s -> ${d.ep} ${JSON.stringify(d.body)}`)

297	  } else {
298	    log(`${bot.name} idle task ${d.ep} rejected: ${JSON.stringify(res)?.slice(0, 120)}`)
299	  }
300	}

input.summary: goal-directed idle engine — design report, recommend Workflow for build
input.message:
Engineer here. Design done, no code written yet. Verdict up front: this smells like Workflow territory for the BUILD (concurrency + a policy change + real ambiguity worth resolving before code) — but I want to flag a naming correction first since it changes where this actually lives.

CORRECTION: "idle-guard" is two different things in this codebase. runner.js's idleGuardCycle (in-process, per-bot) does drop-sweep + deposit-surplus — that's NOT what fires "collect r16, chop 4." The role-default system you're describing is overseer.mjs (orchestrator-side, separate process, BOTS[].defaults array + tick()) — confirmed by reading it directly, the exact "chop count:4"/"collect radius:8-16"/"hunt pig" defaults live there. This design targets overseer.mjs, not runner.js. Flagging now so we're building the right file.

SCHEMA (goals.json), refined from your sketch:
{id, priority (number, higher=first), kind, params (exact existing endpoint body), requires: {items?: [{name,minCount}], zone?: string, minDurability?: number}, repeat: bool, claimedBy?: string, claimedAt?: ISO-ts}

ALGORITHM (overseer.mjs tick(), before the existing role-default fallback):
1. Load goals.json fresh each tick (cheap file read + mtime-cache — picks up your live edits without a restart).
2. Auto-unclaim stale entries: claimedAt older than ~5min AND that bot's current task doesn't match the claim → force-unclaim (crash/restart safety, same spirit as runner.js's idle-guard safety-TTL I built earlier today — a claim must never survive an overseer restart forever).
3. Filter goals to: unclaimed, requires satisfied against st.inventory/st.pos (cheap, already-fetched /status data — your G1 durability/heldItem work from today lands right here for minDurability checks).
4. Sort by priority desc, stable by id; pick first eligible; skip re-picking the bot's own immediately-prior goal id if a different eligible one exists (avoids one repeat:true goal looping a bot forever when other work's available).
5. Claim (write goals.json back with claimedBy+claimedAt), fire via existing api() helper, log to a new cave/goal-picks.jsonl (flat file, gitignored, same append-tolerant pattern as ledger/missions) + grey() Discord line "idle→goal: <id>".
6. On a LATER tick (task completion is only visible on the next poll, overseer doesn't await it), detect done/failed for a goal-claimed bot (extend the in-memory state Map with activeGoalId) → unclaim in goals.json; repeat:false entries get removed entirely on success.
7. Nothing eligible → unchanged fallback to the existing BOTS[].defaults rotation.

SAFETY, unchanged from today's doctrine: one-commander preserved (still only fires on a bot with NO running task, still never force:true — identical gate to the current code); dig-law is enforced where it already lives (mine's own isInDigZone, my new zone param) — the engine just calls the same endpoints, doesn't reimplement any law.

3 OPEN QUESTIONS I resolved with a judgment call, flagging for your confirmation rather than silently assuming:
1. `requires.zone` — read as "bot must currently be at/near this zone" (workstation-affinity gate, keeps miners near their post), DISTINCT from `params.zone` (the /mine call's own target-zone constraint, my feature from today). Same field name, two different jobs — say if you want a different split.
2. Furnace "free" for the smelt chain — there's no code-queryable lock, USING/FREE is a chat-lease convention (BASE.md doctrine), not structured state. Designed the engine to NOT try to verify this itself — it only checks the BOT's own readiness (has raw_iron+coal on hand). You (as goals.json curator) toggle a smelt entry's presence/priority based on real lease state you're already tracking. Engine doesn't parse chat/leases — that's a much bigger, fragile addition I'd want a separate call on if you actually want it automated.
3. `depth-capable` in your sketch — genuinely unclear to me what signal this checks (equipped torches/food tier? a hardcoded per-bot flag like the current miner-exclusion list?). Didn't guess — need your definition before this can be requires-checked at all.

POLICY CALL-OUT, not a design detail, wanted it explicit: your iron-chain goal set re-enables auto-mining (branchmine segments) for bots currently hard-excluded from any auto-mine default (Thak/Durk/Mog, "DIG LAW — miners excluded" in overseer.mjs's own header, added after 2 real incidents). That exclusion predates today's safety fixes (dig-support 0b2eee7, zone-filter 0dca76b, reach-gap, canDig:false) which do close the specific holes that caused those incidents — so lifting it now is defensible, but it IS a deliberate risk-posture change, not a neutral refactor. Just don't want it to land as a side effect of the goal-engine work without you having said "yes, lift it" out loud.

Recommend: Workflow for the build once questions 1-3 are answered — real concurrency (claim/unclaim across ticks + file writes), a genuine policy change, and enough open surface area that a design-then-build split earns its keep here. Ready to seed the Workflow with this design as context, or take a narrower solo slice first (e.g. just the schema + claim/unclaim mechanics + goal-picks logging, leaving the actual goals.json content and mining-policy question for a follow-up) if you'd rather de-risk incrementally. Your call.

input.message:
Folded in, two things worth flagging before this goes to a Workflow.

GOOD FIT: "banked" stock levels need a cheap, no-bot-dispatch-needed data source for overseer.mjs to compute deficits from. cave/ledger/*.jsonl (today's work) is exactly that — sum deltas per item across all bot files = current banked total, milliseconds, already on disk, zero new infra. Nice validation that the ledger wasn't just a nice-to-have. One real caveat to carry forward: this tracks CHEST transactions specifically (matches "banked" precisely), but accuracy depends on drivers actually sending DEPOT lines for every real deposit/withdraw — already a standing law, not a new risk, just noting the dependency. Priority formula I'd propose: hard floor trigger at `current < min` (no goal below that), severity scales as `(target - current) / target` so iron's big min→target gap naturally outranks a stock that's only slightly under.

GAP FOUND: the tool re-kit pseudo-goal ("withdraw/craft replacement") doesn't cleanly map to an existing HTTP endpoint. ensureTool is an internal skills.js helper other skills call into (mineBlocks/chopTrees/branchMine), never exposed on its own — there's no /ensureTool or equivalent a bare re-kit task could fire. Two ways to close it: (a) small new endpoint exposing ensureTool directly (bounded, matches an existing internal pattern, straightforward), or (b) the pseudo-goal fires a /withdraw attempt from chest B first, checks durability again next tick, falls back to /craft if still low — no new endpoint, but spreads one logical action across 2 idle ticks and is messier to reason about. I'd lean (a) — cheap, and it's a capability worth having exposed regardless of this feature.

Still holding on code — haven't heard back on the 3 open questions (requires.zone split, furnace-lease handling, depth-capable definition) or the Workflow-vs-solo-slice call. This addendum reinforces the Workflow lean (dynamic ledger-driven priority computation + a new endpoint both add real surface). Ready whenever you want to greenlight either path.

content.content:
1	# BARITONE.md — heavy-lifter bots: headless real-client + Baritone
2	
3	Blueprint for adding Baritone-driven REAL Minecraft Java clients alongside the
4	mineflayer fleet. Mineflayer stays primary; baritone bots are ADDITIONAL
5	heavy-lifters for long-haul pathing, bulk mining, and big travel. Prototype
6	bot: **BariBrute**.
7	
8	Decision date: 2026-09-01. Verdict: **PATH 1 — HeadlessMc + official Baritone
9	v1.17.0** (real cabaletta release, built FOR 1.21.11, Fabric supported).
10	Community forks (Nevarielle, chasteboymc-boop) are obsolete — skip. Minosoft
11	(no baritone hook) and Automatone (server-side mod, violates client-only
12	spirit) rejected.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Chosen stack — exact versions + URLs
17	
18	| Component | Version | URL |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar` |
21	| Baritone (official, standalone fabric) | v1.17.0 | `https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` |
22	| hmc-specifics (console→game control wire) | 1.21.11-fabric, mod 2.4.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar` |
23	| Fabric API | match 1.21.11 (~0.141.3+1.21.11) | pull via HMC `mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api` (Modrinth) — safer than hand-URL |
24	| Java | 21 (already installed) | `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe` |
25	
26	Fallback if hmc-specifics jar clashes with baritone at mod load (rare): drop
27	hmc-specifics, relaunch with `-commands` flag (built-in headlessmc-runtime,
28	weaker console — basic chat send still works). That is PATH 2; try only if
29	PATH 1 breaks.
30	
31	Known non-issue: server-side plugin "BaritoneRemover" exists in the wild and
32	kicks baritone users — irrelevant here, our own localhost server, not
33	installed.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. Install layout — `C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\`
38	
39	Per-bot directory = per-bot game dir. Each launcher runs with cwd set to its
40	bot dir so `.minecraft\logs\latest.log` (the state channel) and
41	`.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` are isolated per bot. Disk cost of the
42	duplicated version files is accepted for isolation.
43	
44	```
45	C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\
46	  baritone-runner.mjs                  <- HTTP wrapper (this blueprint, part 4)
47	  shared\                              <- downloaded jars, copied into each bot
48	    headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
49	    baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
50	    hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
51	  bots\BariBrute\                      <- cwd for BariBrute's launcher process
52	    headlessmc-launcher.jar            (copy from shared)
53	    .minecraft\
54	      mods\                            (fabric-api + baritone + hmc-specifics)
55	      logs\latest.log                  (state channel — wrapper tails this)
56	      baritone\settings.txt            (safety config, pre-written by wrapper)
57	  pids\  logs\                         <- wrapper-level, same shape as cave/
58	```
59	
60	### Install steps (one-time, PowerShell)
61	
62	```powershell
63	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
64	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\BariBrute
65	cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
66	curl.exe -L -o headlessmc-launcher.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
67	curl.exe -L -o baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
68	curl.exe -L -o hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
69	copy headlessmc-launcher.jar ..\bots\BariBrute\
70	
71	# interactive first-run inside bot dir (installs fabric + fabric-api):
72	cd ..\bots\BariBrute
73	& "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe" -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar
74	```
75	
76	Inside the HMC console, one line at a time:
77	
78	```
79	config --property hmc.offline.username=BariBrute
80	fabric 1.21.11
81	mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api
82	specifics fabric:1.21.11 hmc-specifics
83	```
84	
85	If `specifics` doesn't know 1.21.11 yet, hand-copy instead. Baritone always
86	needs hand-copy (not on Modrinth):
87	
88	```powershell
89	copy ..\..\shared\baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar .minecraft\mods\
90	copy ..\..\shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar .minecraft\mods\   # only if specifics cmd failed
91	```
92	
93	### Launch line (what the wrapper sends after boot, or manual test)
94	
95	```
96	launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline -lwjgl --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Djava.awt.headless=true" --game-args "--quickPlayMultiplayer localhost:25565"
97	```
98	
99	- `-offline` + `hmc.offline.username` = no Microsoft OAuth (server is
100	  offline-mode, matches).
101	- `-lwjgl` = headless LWJGL patch, no window.
102	- `--quickPlayMultiplayer` = auto-join, zero GUI clicking.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## 3. Control + feedback channels
107	
108	**Command wire (in):** launcher process stdin. hmc-specifics adds console
109	words once the game is loaded: `msg <text>` (send chat exactly like a player),
110	plus `connect`/`disconnect` and `/` for slash commands. A `#`-prefixed chat
111	line is intercepted CLIENT-SIDE by Baritone (`chatControl` setting, on by
112	default) before it leaves for the server — baritone commands never appear in
113	real server chat.
114	
115	```
116	msg #goto 100 64 200
117	msg #mine 64 iron_ore
118	msg #stop
119	```
120	
121	**Feedback wire (out):** NOT the HMC console — the client's own
122	`.minecraft\logs\latest.log`. Baritone replies go to the local chat HUD only,
123	and vanilla logs HUD lines with the `[CHAT]` marker. Tail that file, regex:
124	
125	```
126	/\[CHAT\].*?\[(Baritone|B)\]\s*(.+)/
127	```
128	
129	At boot send `msg #set chatDebug true` for coordinate-bearing path/segment
130	debug lines (BetterBlockPos-shaped `(x,y,z)` text upstream — FIELD-VERIFY the
131	exact 1.17.0 string once live). Fallback position poll: `msg #eta` every few
132	seconds while a task runs, parse the reply line.
133	
134	Baritone command surface (verified from cabaletta USAGE.md): `#goto x y z`,
135	`#goal`/`#path`, `#mine <count> <ore>`, `#follow <player>`, `#farm [range]`,
136	`#tunnel [h] [w] [d]`, `#build <schematic>`, `#explore`, `#stop`/`#cancel`/
137	`#forcecancel`, `#wp save/goal`, `#come`, `#find`, `#eta`, `#proc`. `#farm`
138	args beyond `<range> <waypoint>` unverified — field-check.
139	
140	**No RCON anywhere in this path.** Commands in via client stdin-fed chat,
141	state out via client's own log file. The only RCON touch remains the
142	orchestrator's later cosmetic `team join` for the BariBrute name tag —
143	separate process, never through this wrapper. LAW.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## 4. Wrapper design — `baritone-runner.mjs`
148	
149	Same shape as `cave/runner.js`: one process per bot, HTTP control API on
150	127.0.0.1, state polled not pushed. Difference: no in-process mineflayer
151	object — this is a **process-pipe + log-tail driver** around an external JVM.
152	
153	```
154	node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 [--host localhost --mcport 25565]
155	```
156	
157	**Port registry:** baritone heavy-lifters own **3301-3309** (mineflayer keeps
158	3200-3299 per CIV.md — add a cross-note there). BariBrute = 3301.
159	
160	**Boot sequence:**
161	1. Pre-write `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` with the safety block (part 5)
162	   — config-file level, survives relaunch, no chat-push race.
163	2. `spawn('C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-21.0.10\\bin\\java.exe', ['-jar','headlessmc-launcher.jar'], { cwd: BOT_DIR, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] })`
164	3. Write the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line (part 2) to stdin.
165	4. Start log tail (fs.watch + read-from-last-offset on
166	   `.minecraft\logs\latest.log`); wait for join marker before accepting tasks.
167	5. Send `msg #set chatDebug true`.
168	
169	**HTTP surface (mirrors cave/runner.js task-endpoint shape):**
170	
171	| Endpoint | Body | Action |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /goto` | `{x,y,z}` | no-go gate → `msg #goto x y z` |
174	| `POST /mine` | `{block,count}` | `msg #mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings) |
175	| `POST /tunnel` | `{h,w,d}` | no-go gate on projected end → `msg #tunnel h w d` |
176	| `POST /farm` | `{range}` | `msg #farm <range>` |
177	| `POST /follow` | `{player}` | `msg #follow <player>` |
178	| `POST /stop` | — | `msg #stop` |
179	| `POST /relog` | — | hmc-specifics `disconnect` + `connect`; full JVM relaunch if that fails |
180	| `GET /status` | — | `{name, position, task, lastBaritoneLine, connected, uptime}` from parsed log state |
181	
182	`/status` and `/stop` semantics match what `overseer.mjs` already polls, so
183	the overseer can adopt BariBrute with one BOTS-array row (part 6).
184	
185	---
186	
187	## 5. Safety config
188	
189	### 5a. Boot settings — written to `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt`
190	
191	```
192	legitMine true                # honest visible-only mining, no X-ray scan
193	allowDownward false           # never mine block under own feet (fall-safety, matches fleet doctrine)
194	minYLevelWhileMining -54      # floor: stay above bedrock chaos
195	maxYLevelWhileMining 95       # ceiling: all ore-hunting stays BELOW both bases (camp y~89 surface, FEL y=111)
196	blocksToDisallowBreaking [chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel]
197	shortBaritonePrefix true      # "[B]" — stable short tag for the log regex
198	chatDebug true                # belt+braces with the boot msg push
199	```
200	
201	### 5b. FEL no-go zone (-3, 111, 4) ±15 — WRAPPER-LEVEL, MANDATORY
202	
203	**Baritone has NO native coordinate keep-out zone.** Verified upstream:
204	issues #2597 ("Blacklisted zones"), #3847 ("safearea/No break zone"), #1165
205	("Blacklisting coordinates") — all open, never shipped. `#blacklist` only
206	skips the single closest matched block; `#sel` is a build-area selector, not
207	an exclusion. So the wrapper enforces, two layers:
208	
209	**Layer 1 — command gate.** Every coordinate-bearing task (`/goto`, `/tunnel`
210	projected end, future `/goal`) is checked before piping. Reject with HTTP 403
211	if the target lands inside the padded full-height column:
212	
213	```js
214	const NOGO = { x: -3, z: 4, r: 15, pad: 5 };   // padded box: x [-23,17], z [-16,24], all y
215	function inNoGo(x, z) {
216	  return x >= NOGO.x - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && x <= NOGO.x + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad
217	      && z >= NOGO.z - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && z <= NOGO.z + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad;
218	}
219	```
220	
221	Full-height column (not a y-slab): break-capable pathing under or over the
222	FEL base is foundation risk, not worth the shortcut.
223	
224	**Layer 2 — position watchdog.** `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` take no coords
225	and a legal `#goto` can still PATH THROUGH the zone (baritone cannot be told
226	to route around it). So the log-tail position parser doubles as watchdog:
227	parsed position inside the padded box → immediately `msg #stop`, then
228	`msg #goto <camp waypoint>`, mark task `aborted:nogo` in `/status`, log loud.
229	Watchdog is the backstop; the gate is the front door. Drivers should also
230	prefer targets whose straight line to the bot doesn't cross the box.
231	
232	### 5c. Standing laws inherited from the fleet
233	
234	- NO RCON world commands from wrapper or driver, ever.
235	- Team tag = orchestrator RCON `team join CAVE BariBrute` later, cosmetic
236	  only, allowed.
237	- Stupid-funny naming law: BariBrute, future siblings same spirit
238	  (BariBonk, LiftLug...).
239	
240	---
241	
242	## 6. RAM budget
243	
244	| Item | Each | Count | Total |
245	|---|---|---|---|
246	| MC headless client (`-Xmx3G`, working set 1.5-3GB) | 3.0 GB worst | 2 | 6.0 GB |
247	| HMC launcher JVM | 0.2 GB | 2 | 0.4 GB |
248	| baritone-runner.mjs node | 0.05 GB | 2 | 0.1 GB |
249	| mineflayer runners (existing) | ~0.35 GB | 8 | 2.8 GB |
250	| overseer + misc node | — | — | 0.3 GB |
251	| **Total fleet** | | | **~9.6 GB** |
252	
253	Against 21 GB free: fits with ~11 GB headroom. **Law: max 2 baritone bots**
254	alongside the 8-bot mineflayer fleet. A third only if measured working sets
255	come in under 2 GB each after a real mining session.
256	
257	---
258	
259	## 7. Integration
260	
261	- **overseer.mjs:** add `{ name: 'BariBrute', port: 3301, color: 'dark_red', kind: 'baritone' }`
262	  to BOTS. `/status` + `/stop` + `/relog` already line up. Guard
263	  mineflayer-only autopilot moves (deposit chores, teleport-to-spawn) behind
264	  `kind !== 'baritone'` — baritone recovery = `/stop` + `/relog` only.
265	- **CIV.md:** port-registry note "3301-3309 = baritone heavy-lifters (see
266	  BARITONE.md)" + roster row BariBrute / 3301 / heavy-lift miner-hauler /
267	  BariBruteDriver / planned.
268	- **TODO.md:** this is row #14 (wf_dd72675c). On prototype green: mark DONE,
269	  add follow-up rows (BariBrute first bulk job; orchestrator team-tag).
270	- **Drivers:** BariBruteDriver talks HTTP exactly like other drivers, per
271	  DRIVER_GUIDE.md conventions; task vocabulary is the part-4 table.
272	
273	## 8. Field-verify checklist (prototype session)
274	
275	1. hmc-specifics + baritone coexist at mod load (else PATH 2 `-commands`).
276	2. Exact `[B]`/`[Baritone]` chatDebug line format in latest.log → pin regex.
277	3. `#farm` argument shape.
278	4. `msg` vs `.` alias behavior in HMC 2.10.0 console.
279	5. Real working-set RSS after 30 min of `#mine` (updates part-6 table).
280	6. Log rotation: does a `/relog` rotate latest.log (tail must reopen).
281	
282	---
283	
284	## Upstream status 2026-09-01
285	
286	Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
287	to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
288	forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform
289	in minecraft:blur/0" through "blur/5"; (2) hmc-specifics' JLine console
290	misbehaves when stdio is a plain pipe (no TTY), as the wrapper needs.
291	
292	### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms
293	
294	Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
295	uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
296	grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
297	`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
298	non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
299	bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
300	to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
301	and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
302	abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
303	(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
304	come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).
305	
306	Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
307	release:
308	- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
309	  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
310	  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
311	  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
312	  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
313	  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
314	  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
315	  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
316	- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
317	  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
318	  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
319	- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
320	  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
321	  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
322	- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
323	  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
324	- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
325	  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
326	  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
327	  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
328	  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
329	- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
330	  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
331	  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
332	  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.
333	
334	**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
335	own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
336	patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
337	More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
338	real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
339	over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
340	real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
341	gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
342	game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
343	redirection layer at all.
344	- hmc-specifics' console (`msg`, `connect`, `gui`, `click`) is confirmed to
345	  work identically with or without `-lwjgl` — see maintainer replies in
346	  [issue #230](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/230) and
347	  [issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390). Baritone
348	  chat-command control (part 3 of this doc) is unaffected by dropping the
349	  flag.
350	- Trade-off: a real (small, minimizable) game window per bot instance, and a
351	  sliver of real GPU/VRAM per client instead of zero. JVM heap budget in part
352	  6 is unaffected (that's CPU RAM, not GPU).
353	- If this stack ever moves to a true headless Linux box with no GPU at all,
354	  the Linux-native equivalent is Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe (software GL) in front
355	  of an un-patched launch — a working docker recipe is in
356	  [issue #249](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/249) (needs
357	  the `x11-xserver-utils` package per maintainer 3arthqu4ke, plus
358	  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Not directly usable on bare Windows (no X11);
359	  would need WSL2. Untested by this pass — field-verify separately if needed.
360	- If dropping `-lwjgl` is rejected and true headless is a hard requirement:
361	  this bucket is "fixable soon, not now" — file a new upstream issue with the
362	  exact blur/uniform log lines + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric. The
363	  maintainers (okafke, 3arthqu4ke) have a strong track record on this exact
364	  bug family — #388/#389 to merged fixes #406/#407 the same day.
365	
366	### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)
367	
368	Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
369	[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
370	"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
371	reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
372	reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
373	`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
374	section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").
375	
376	Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
377	`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
378	separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
379	guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
380	is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
381	that way.
382	
383	`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
384	one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
385	a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
386	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
387	  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
388	  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
389	- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
390	  version of the above.
391	
392	No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
393	ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
394	maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
395	reason to stand up a pty shim.
396	
397	**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
398	(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
399	from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.
400	
401	### Alternatives sanity check
402	
403	- **Automatone** ([Ladysnake/Automatone](https://github.com/Ladysnake/Automatone),
404	  active, last updated 2026-07-10) — confirmed dead end for this stack, as
405	  suspected. It's a **server-side Fabric mod**: you attach Baritone pathing to
406	  any entity via a Java `EntityComponentFactory` registered server-side
407	  (`BaritoneAPI.getProvider().getBaritone(entity)`), driven entirely by
408	  in-process Java API calls. There is no protocol-level or console/chat
409	  control surface at all — mineflayer (an external protocol client) has
410	  nothing to hook into. Not usable, full stop.
411	- No other maintained "real headless Java client + baritone" project exists
412	  for 1.21.x besides HeadlessMc + hmc-specifics + official Baritone (PATH 1,
413	  already chosen). Official Baritone itself is healthy and current:
414	  [cabaletta/baritone releases](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases)
415	  show v1.16.0 (1.21.9/1.21.10), **v1.17.0 (1.21.11 — ours)**, v1.18.0 (26.1),
416	  v1.19.0 (26.2) — all four pushed 2026-08-31, one release per MC version,
417	  no drama.
418	- `Nevarielle/baritone-1.21.11` (community fork) still exists but is now
419	  redundant — official v1.17.0 covers 1.21.11 directly. Matches this doc's
420	  existing "obsolete — skip" call, no change needed.
421	
422	### Verdict
423	
424	- **Blocker 1 (render hang): fixable now, not via any HMC flag/release, but
425	  via a launch-config change — drop `-lwjgl`, run BariBrute's client with a
426	  real (minimized) window on the real GPU.** This sidesteps HeadlessMc's
427	  incomplete RenderPipeline/uniform emulation, the near-certain cause, which
428	  is not fixed or even filed upstream for the blur pipeline specifically
429	  (2.9.0/2.10.0 only fixed the neighboring memSlice-NPE and 26.2 DeviceLimits
430	  gaps). If a fully invisible process is a hard requirement, this drops to
431	  "fixable soon" — file upstream and wait; track record is good but nothing
432	  to point to yet.
433	- **Blocker 2 (JLine over plain pipe): fixable now** via config property, no
434	  pty wrapper needed — `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first, else the
435	  confirmed `hmc.jline.enabled=false` from issue #390. Keep never using
436	  `-commands` alongside hmc-specifics.
437	- **Alternatives: no change to PATH 1.** Automatone is confirmed unusable
438	  (server-side Java-API-only, no external-bot hook); official Baritone
439	  v1.17.0 for 1.21.11 remains current and healthy.
440	
441	### Exact next actions
442	
443	1. Drop `-lwjgl` from the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line in parts 2 and 4.
444	   Keep `-offline`. Add a small window size and OS-level minimize/off-screen
445	   placement in the wrapper's boot sequence in place of the render patch.
446	2. Add `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` to HMC's `config.properties` (or
447	   as a launch `-D` JVM arg). Only if console commands still misbehave over
448	   the wrapper's stdio pipe, switch to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` instead.
449	3. Do not add `-commands` anywhere — hmc-specifics alone is the console
450	   surface (maintainer guidance, issue #390).
451	4. If `-lwjgl` is ever required again (e.g. a true headless Linux box with no
452	   GPU), come back to this section and pursue Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe per the
453	   docker recipe in issue #249 — untested by this pass, field-verify
454	   separately.
455	5. Optional, only if committed to keeping true `-lwjgl` headless long-term:
456	   file a new issue on headlesshq/headlessmc with the exact blur/uniform log
457	   excerpt + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric, citing the memSlice/DeviceLimits
458	   precedent in this section to speed triage.
459	
460	---
461	
462	## Round 2 field session 2026-09-01 — verdict: WORKS (see final update below)
463	
464	Applied both prescribed fixes from the section above and pushed BariBrute
465	through a real launch on real hardware (AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, no `-lwjgl`).
466	Made real progress, hit a new, different, previously-undocumented stall.
467	Full verdict: **blocked tonight — needs either a visible window or an
468	upstream/config fix not yet found — leaving as a decision for the morning.**
469	
470	### What actually got fixed this round (real progress, keep these)
471	
472	1. **Baritone was never actually installed in round 1.** `baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar`
473	   had been downloaded to `shared\` but never copied into any mods folder any
474	   attempted launch actually used — confirmed by grepping every round-1
475	   launch log's `Fabric Mods:` dump, which lists `fabric-api`/`headlessmc`/
476	   `minecraft` only, no `baritone` entry anywhere. Fixed by copying both
477	   `baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` and the specifics-installed
478	   `hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar` into the **global**
479	   `%APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods\` (confirmed HMC 2.10.0 always uses this one
480	   global profile regardless of launcher cwd, per the existing note in
481	   `baritone-runner.mjs`). Result: `Loading 51 mods: ... - baritone 1.17.0
482	   \-- dev_babbaj_nether-pathfinder 1.6 ...` — mod loads clean now.
483	2. **`config --property hmc.offline.username=...` never persisted.** HMC
484	   prints `Not running from the headlessmc-launcher-wrapper. No plugin
485	   support and in-memory launching.` at boot — config-command changes made
486	   through the console are in-memory only without that wrapper, so every
487	   fresh launcher process (a new `java -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar`) lost
488	   them. Round 1's actual launches all show `--username Offline` on the
489	   child JVM command line despite the bootstrap script successfully running
490	   `config --property hmc.offline.username=BariBrute` first. **Fix:** write
491	   `hmc.offline.username=BariBrute` directly into
492	   `bots\BariBrute\HeadlessMC\config.properties` on disk before launching,
493	   bypassing the runtime command entirely. Confirmed working: child JVM
494	   cmdline now shows `--username BariBrute`.
495	3. **Dropping `-lwjgl` confirmed correct per the section above** — every
496	   round-2 launch reached real GPU rendering (`Render thread` creating
497	   texture atlases, harmless one-time `blur/0`-`blur/5` uniform WARNs) with
498	   no crash from the render side. Blocker 1 from the prior research pass is
499	   resolved.
500	
501	### New blocker found this round — hmc-specifics' own in-game JLine reader
502	
503	With `-lwjgl` dropped and both mods loaded, the very first real launch
504	(`hmc-launch4.mjs`) crashed immediately after mod init, **inside the game
505	JVM itself**, before reaching the render thread:
506	
507	```
508	java.lang.IllegalStateException: Failed to start JLineCommandLineReader
509	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.jline.VersionAgnosticJLineCommandLineReader.installAndReadAsyncAndAwaitException
510	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.SpecificsInitializer.readCommandLine
511	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.SpecificsInitializer.init
512	  at net.minecraft.class_310.handler$bck000$headlessmc$onInit   <- mixin into Minecraft's own constructor
513	Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Failed to call new JLineProviders!
514	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.jline.NewJLineProviders.provide
515	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.jline.VersionAgnosticJLineCommandLineReader.hackInTerminal
516	```
517	
518	Root cause, confirmed: **this is a second, separate JLine console — inside
519	the GAME process itself**, distinct from the launcher's own JLine (which
520	already auto-negotiates `dumb` terminal mode fine over the piped stdin, per
521	`headlessmc.log`: `JLine Terminal type: dumb`). Under PATH 1 (hmc-specifics,
522	no `-commands`), hmc-specifics mixes into `Minecraft.<init>` and spins up
523	*another* JLine reader inside the child JVM to read further stdin — and this
524	one is NOT auto-falling back to dumb mode, so it crashes trying to build a
525	real Windows console terminal over what is, from the child JVM's point of
526	view, a fully piped/non-console stdin (the launcher relays commands to it,
527	the child JVM's own stdin isn't a real console handle at all).
528	
529	Two upstream fixes attempted, from this doc's own recommended order:
530	
531	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true`, passed as a `--jvm -D` flag on the
532	  `launch` line (confirmed present verbatim in the child JVM's actual
533	  cmdline via `headlessmc.log`'s `ProcessFactory` entry) — **did not help,
534	  identical crash, same stack trace.** The dumb-mode flag doesn't prevent
535	  the crash; whatever this code path does, it fails before or regardless of
536	  checking that property.
537	- `hmc.jline.enabled=false`, same way (`--jvm "-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"`)
538	  — **this worked.** No crash. Game proceeded past `SpecificsInitializer.init`
539	  straight through mod loading, asset/texture atlas creation, and the
540	  blur-uniform WARNs, into a live render loop. This is the confirmed fix for
541	  this blocker — use `hmc.jline.enabled=false` directly, don't bother trying
542	  the dumb-mode flag first for this exact crash (leave the recommendation in
543	  the section above as-is for the general JLine-over-pipe case; this specific
544	  in-game-JLine-during-Minecraft-init crash needs the harder disable).
545	
546	**Doc update:** for PATH 1 (hmc-specifics loaded), pass
547	`-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false` on the `--jvm` launch flag from the very first
548	attempt. `config.properties`-level settings do not reliably reach the child
549	game JVM's flags (only some launcher-level settings like offline username
550	do) — always prefer the `--jvm -D` route for anything that needs to affect
551	the spawned Minecraft process specifically.
552	
553	### Third blocker found this round — game stalls forever, never attempts to join, window-visibility-independent
554	
555	With both above fixes applied (baritone+specifics installed, offline
556	username persisted, `hmc.jline.enabled=false`), the game **no longer
557	crashes** but also **never connects**. It reaches the render loop, logs the
558	harmless Realms-auth-401 and `blur/0`-`blur/5` WARNs, and then goes
559	completely silent — no `Connecting to`, no `Encryption`, no world-load line,
560	nothing — while the process stays alive, "responding" flickers between
561	`Running`/`Not Responding` in `tasklist`, and CPU time creeps up by roughly
562	1 second of CPU per 30-40 seconds of wall time (consistent with an idle
563	title-screen render loop doing near-nothing, not a deadlock or a spin).
564	`jstack` on the stalled process during the first occurrence confirmed the
565	render thread is in a completely ordinary `Thread.sleep` inside
566	`Minecraft.render`/`run` (`class_310.method_1523`/`method_1514`) — i.e. it
567	genuinely is just idling at whatever screen it's on, not blocked/deadlocked
568	on anything catchable in a thread dump. `--quickPlayMultiplayer
569	localhost:25565` never appears to fire, or fires and fails completely
570	silently with zero log trace either way.
571	
572	This was reproduced **twice, identically**, under two different window-
573	visibility strategies, ruling out the visibility angle as the cause:
574	
575	1. **Fully hidden window** (`ShowWindowAsync(hwnd, SW_HIDE)` applied to any
576	   new java window once created) — stalled at this exact point, confirmed
577	   via live `jstack` thread dump (killed by the coordinator after ~170s
578	   observed with zero progress).
579	2. **Minimized window** (`ShowWindowAsync(hwnd, SW_MINIMIZE)` instead,
580	   theorized as safer since DWM keeps compositing/presenting minimized
581	   windows unlike fully hidden ones) — **stalled identically**, same log
582	   line count frozen at the same `blur/5` point, same slow CPU creep, no
583	   RCON-visible join after 90+ seconds of polling. This falsifies the
584	   "hidden window starves the GPU swapchain" hypothesis from earlier in this
585	   session — minimized behaves the same as hidden, so window visibility
586	   state is not the variable causing the stall.
587	
588	Neither attempt ever produced a visible client window at any point (both
589	began life immediately with the window creation followed within ~3s by a
590	hide/minimize pass), so the no-visible-client law was never violated by this
591	session, and both attempts were killed cleanly with no client left
592	connected or visible.
593	
594	**What this narrows the cause down to** (untested, for the next session):
595	something in the PATH 1 stack (hmc-specifics init running inside
596	`Minecraft.<init>` via mixin, possibly interacting with how quickPlay is
597	scheduled relative to that mixin hook) either never fires the quickPlay
598	auto-connect at all, or fires it into a silent failure. Candidates worth
599	testing next, cheapest first:
600	- Manual connect instead of relying on `--quickPlayMultiplayer`: once the
601	  hmc-specifics console is confirmed alive in-game (it should be, since the
602	  crash that used to block it is fixed), drive it with `msg #include`... no
603	  — more directly, use the vanilla `connect <host>` hmc-specifics console
604	  word (or navigate the menu via `click`/`gui` console words documented for
605	  hmc-specifics) instead of the `--quickPlayMultiplayer` game arg, to see if
606	  the stall is specific to the quickPlay code path vs. multiplayer joining
607	  in general.
608	- Compare against PATH 2 (`-commands`, no hmc-specifics) with `-lwjgl`
609	  dropped: round 1's `hmc-launch2.mjs`/`hmc-launch3.mjs` runs (PATH 2, no
610	  baritone installed at the time) reached the exact same `blur/5` point and
611	  were also never confirmed to actually join before being externally killed
612	  — so this stall may predate this round's PATH-1-specific changes entirely
613	  and be a `--quickPlayMultiplayer` + HeadlessMc issue in general, not
614	  specific to hmc-specifics. Re-test PATH 2 now that baritone/mods are
615	  correctly installed, to isolate whether hmc-specifics is actually involved
616	  at all.
617	- Try omitting `--quickPlayMultiplayer` entirely and driving a manual
618	  multiplayer connect through hmc-specifics' `click`/`gui` console words
619	  once at the title screen, to bypass whatever quickPlay's internal state
620	  machine is stuck on.
621	- Capture a `jstack` dump specifically at the moment `--quickPlayMultiplayer`
622	  should be firing (right after title screen init) rather than after the
623	  fact, to see if a connect thread is present but parked, vs. never spawned.
624	
625	### Cleanup performed
626	
627	All BariBrute-round-2 java/node processes killed (launcher, game JVM, and
628	the `hmc-launch7.mjs` node wrapper) — verified via `tasklist`/`Get-Process`
629	that no stray processes remain and that the real server (PID 13908,
630	`fabric-server-launch`) was never touched. Left in place for next session
631	(real progress, do not undo): the mods copied into
632	`%APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods\` (`baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar`,
633	`hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar`), and
634	`bots\BariBrute\HeadlessMC\config.properties`'s added
635	`hmc.offline.username=BariBrute` / `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true`
636	lines (harmless even though the dumb-mode one didn't end up mattering).
637	`hmc-launch4.mjs` through `hmc-launch7.mjs` in `baritone-lifter\` record the
638	exact progression of fixes tried, in order, for the next session to resume
639	from `hmc-launch7.mjs`'s approach (drop the window-hide/minimize step first
640	since it's now shown to be irrelevant to the stall; focus directly on the
641	quickPlay-vs-manual-connect question above).
642	
643	**No visible game client was ever left running.** BariBrute is not currently
644	connected to the fleet.
645	
646	---
647	
648	## Round 2 FINAL update — same session, 15-min hard cap — verdict: WORKS
649	
650	Coordinator's last card fixed it. Root cause of the "third blocker" above:
651	**`--quickPlayMultiplayer` itself is the broken piece, not window visibility,
652	not hmc-specifics, not jline.** Fix: drop `--quickPlayMultiplayer` from the
653	`launch` game-args entirely, boot to a plain title screen, then issue a
654	**manual connect** over the hmc-specifics console channel once the title
655	screen is up.
656	
657	### Exact working recipe
658	
659	1. Launch line (no quickPlay arg at all):
660	   ```
661	   launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"
662	   ```
663	2. Wait ~35s for title screen (real GPU render reaches the harmless
664	   blur-uniform WARNs by ~15-20s in; give it another 15s margin).
665	3. Send the connect command over the same stdin pipe:
666	   ```
667	   connect localhost 25565
668	   ```
669	   Exact syntax confirmed by decompiling `ConnectCommand.class` out of
670	   `hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar` with `javap -p -c` (no README/docs
671	   needed): `execute(String label, String... args)` requires `args.length > 1`
672	   ("Please specify an Ip!" otherwise), reads host from `args[1]`, and an
673	   optional port from `args[2]` (default 25565) — i.e. the raw console line is
674	   literally `connect <host> <port>`, space-separated, no flags.
675	4. Confirmed working end to end: client received the server's join/leave
676	   chat spam within ~15s of sending `connect`, and `node swarm/rcon.mjs
677	   "list"` (read-only, from `minecraft-mcp-v2`) showed `BariBrute` in the
678	   player list.
679	
680	**Doc update:** never use `--quickPlayMultiplayer` with this stack on this
681	MC/HMC version. Always boot plain and drive the join manually through
682	hmc-specifics' `connect` console word. This makes the earlier "candidates
683	for next session" list in the previous update moot — the first candidate
684	(manual connect instead of quickPlay) was the fix.
685	
686	### Baritone command channel — field-verified format
687	
688	Sent `msg #goto 60 90 120` over the launcher stdin once joined. Baritone
689	logged its own path plan to the launcher's stdout/log
690	(`[STDOUT]: Path goes for 76.69419795525604 blocks`) and began moving.
691	Confirmed movement via the fleet's own mineflayer bot HTTP eval endpoint
692	(`POST 127.0.0.1:3203/eval`, `bot.players['BariBrute'].entity.position`):
693	position went from `(3.5, 111, -6.5)` at spawn to `(11.97, 94, 48.45)` after
694	the goto fired — moving in the correct direction (x up, y down toward the
695	target's 90, z up toward the target's 120).
696	
697	Sent `msg #stop` next. Baritone answered on the in-game chat feedback
698	channel, format now pinned exactly:
699	```
700	[CHAT] [Baritone] > stop
701	[CHAT] [Baritone] ok canceled
702	```
703	(matches the `/\[CHAT\].*?\[(Baritone|B)\]\s*(.+)/` regex from part 3 of this
704	doc — `[Baritone]`, full word, not the short `[B]` form, at least for this
705	command; `shortBaritonePrefix` config wasn't active in this quick ad-hoc
706	test since it used the bare `launch`/`msg` commands rather than the full
707	`baritone-runner.mjs` wrapper's pre-written settings.txt). Position polled
708	again after `#stop` came back bit-for-bit identical
709	(`11.974708733124642, 94, 48.4548966911917`) confirming a clean, complete
710	halt with zero drift.
711	
712	### Safety incident — spawn point is inside the FEL no-go box, undetected by this ad-hoc script
713	
714	**BariBrute's server spawn point, `(3.5, 111, -6.5)`, is itself inside the
715	FEL no-go padded box** (`x∈[-23,17], z∈[-16,24]`, part 5b of this doc) — y=111
716	matches FEL's own y exactly. The quick `hmc-launch8.mjs` test script used for
717	this session's final attempt is a bare stdin/log-tail script with **no
718	no-go gate and no position watchdog** (those live in `baritone-runner.mjs`,
719	not in the throwaway `hmc-launch*.mjs` scripts used to iterate on the boot
720	sequence this session) — so `#goto 60 90 120` was sent and Baritone started
721	pathing from inside the FEL box with nothing checking it. It was stopped by
722	hand within seconds once the position readback showed the spawn coordinates,
723	before any real distance was covered, but the path was already crossing
724	close by the `[CAVE]` camp waypoint too (`(12, 89, 56)` per this doc's part
725	5c reference) — the position where it was actually stopped,
726	`(11.97, 94, 48.45)`, is only ~9 blocks from that camp point.
727	
728	**Action needed before any unattended/production use:** `baritone-runner.mjs`
729	already has both the no-go gate and the watchdog implemented (part 5b of
730	this doc) — this incident is purely because the quick ad-hoc `hmc-launch8.mjs`
731	test script doesn't wire through it, not a gap in the wrapper design. Next
732	session should either (a) drive BariBrute exclusively through
733	`baritone-runner.mjs` once it's updated with this session's fixes (drop
734	quickPlay, manual `connect`, `hmc.jline.enabled=false`), or (b) manually
735	`#goto` it to a known-clear waypoint immediately after any ad-hoc-script
736	session before leaving it running.
737	
738	### End state
739	
740	BariBrute was left **running and connected**, stopped (not pathing/mining),
741	at `(11.97, 94, 48.45)`. No visible window was shown at any point (hidden
742	via `ShowWindowAsync(SW_HIDE)` on the real GLFW window, applied within ~3s
743	of window creation, same as prior attempts this session).
744	
745	- Launcher java PID: 20240
746	- Game-client java PID: 33944
747	- Node wrapper (`hmc-launch8.mjs`) PID: 11196
748	- Real server (do not touch): PID 13908, untouched throughout
749	
750	**Verdict: WORKS.** Join, `#goto`, movement verification, and `#stop` all

# BARITONE.md — heavy-lifter bots: headless real-client + Baritone

Blueprint for adding Baritone-driven REAL Minecraft Java clients alongside the
mineflayer fleet. Mineflayer stays primary; baritone bots are ADDITIONAL
heavy-lifters for long-haul pathing, bulk mining, and big travel. Prototype
bot: **BariBrute**.

Decision date: 2026-09-01. Verdict: **PATH 1 — HeadlessMc + official Baritone
v1.17.0** (real cabaletta release, built FOR 1.21.11, Fabric supported).
Community forks (Nevarielle, chasteboymc-boop) are obsolete — skip. Minosoft
(no baritone hook) and Automatone (server-side mod, violates client-only
spirit) rejected.

---

## 1. Chosen stack — exact versions + URLs

| Component | Version | URL |
|---|---|---|
| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar` |
| Baritone (official, standalone fabric) | v1.17.0 | `https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` |

## 3. Control + feedback channels

**Command wire (in):** launcher process stdin. hmc-specifics adds console
words once the game is loaded: `msg <text>` (send chat exactly like a player),
plus `connect`/`disconnect` and `/` for slash commands. A `#`-prefixed chat
line is intercepted CLIENT-SIDE by Baritone (`chatControl` setting, on by
default) before it leaves for the server — baritone commands never appear in
real server chat.

```
msg #goto 100 64 200
msg #mine 64 iron_ore
msg #stop
```

**Feedback wire (out):** NOT the HMC console — the client's own
`.minecraft\logs\latest.log`. Baritone replies go to the local chat HUD only,
and vanilla logs HUD lines with the `[CHAT]` marker. Tail that file, regex:

```
/\[CHAT\].*?\[(Baritone|B)\]\s*(.+)/
```

At boot send `msg #set chatDebug true` for coordinate-bearing path/segment
debug lines (BetterBlockPos-shaped `(x,y,z)` text upstream — FIELD-VERIFY the
exact 1.17.0 string once live). Fallback position poll: `msg #eta` every few
seconds while a task runs, parse the reply line.

Baritone command surface (verified from cabaletta USAGE.md): `#goto x y z`,
`#goal`/`#path`, `#mine <count> <ore>`, `#follow <player>`, `#farm [range]`,
`#tunnel [h] [w] [d]`, `#build <schematic>`, `#explore`, `#stop`/`#cancel`/
`#forcecancel`, `#wp save/goal`, `#come`, `#find`, `#eta`, `#proc`. `#farm`
args beyond `<range> <waypoint>` unverified — field-check.

**No RCON anywhere in this path.** Commands in via client stdin-fed chat,
state out via client's own log file. The only RCON touch remains the
orchestrator's later cosmetic `team join` for the BariBrute name tag —
separate process, never through this wrapper. LAW.

## 4. Wrapper design — `baritone-runner.mjs`

Same shape as `cave/runner.js`: one process per bot, HTTP control API on
127.0.0.1, state polled not pushed. Difference: no in-process mineflayer
object — this is a **process-pipe + log-tail driver** around an external JVM.

```
node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 [--host localhost --mcport 25565]
```

**Port registry:** baritone heavy-lifters own **3301-3309** (mineflayer keeps
3200-3299 per CIV.md — add a cross-note there). BariBrute = 3301.

**Boot sequence:**
1. Pre-write `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` with the safety block (part 5)
   — config-file level, survives relaunch, no chat-push race.
2. `spawn('C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-21.0.10\\bin\\java.exe', ['-jar','headlessmc-launcher.jar'], { cwd: BOT_DIR, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] })`
3. Write the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line (part 2) to stdin.
4. Start log tail (fs.watch + read-from-last-offset on
   `.minecraft\logs\latest.log`); wait for join marker before accepting tasks.
5. Send `msg #set chatDebug true`.

**HTTP surface (mirrors cave/runner.js task-endpoint shape):**

| Endpoint | Body | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /goto` | `{x,y,z}` | no-go gate → `msg #goto x y z` |
| `POST /mine` | `{block,count}` | `msg #mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings) |
| `POST /tunnel` | `{h,w,d}` | no-go gate on projected end → `msg #tunnel h w d` |
| `POST /farm` | `{range}` | `msg #farm <range>` |
| `POST /follow` | `{player}` | `msg #follow <player>` |
| `POST /stop` | — | `msg #stop` |
| `POST /relog` | — | hmc-specifics `disconnect` + `connect`; full JVM relaunch if that fails |
| `GET /status` | — | `{name, position, task, lastBaritoneLine, connected, uptime}` from parsed log state |

`/status` and `/stop` semantics match what `overseer.mjs` already polls, so
the overseer can adopt BariBrute with one BOTS-array row (part 6).

## 5. Safety config

### 5a. Boot settings — written to `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt`

```
legitMine true                # honest visible-only mining, no X-ray scan
allowDownward false           # never mine block under own feet (fall-safety, matches fleet doctrine)
minYLevelWhileMining -54      # floor: stay above bedrock chaos
maxYLevelWhileMining 95       # ceiling: all ore-hunting stays BELOW both bases (camp y~89 surface, FEL y=111)
blocksToDisallowBreaking [chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel]
shortBaritonePrefix true      # "[B]" — stable short tag for the log regex
chatDebug true                # belt+braces with the boot msg push
```

### 5b. FEL no-go zone (-3, 111, 4) ±15 — WRAPPER-LEVEL, MANDATORY

**Baritone has NO native coordinate keep-out zone.** Verified upstream:
issues #2597 ("Blacklisted zones"), #3847 ("safearea/No break zone"), #1165
("Blacklisting coordinates") — all open, never shipped. `#blacklist` only
skips the single closest matched block; `#sel` is a build-area selector, not
an exclusion. So the wrapper enforces, two layers:

**Layer 1 — command gate.** Every coordinate-bearing task (`/goto`, `/tunnel`
projected end, future `/goal`) is checked before piping. Reject with HTTP 403
if the target lands inside the padded full-height column:

```js
const NOGO = { x: -3, z: 4, r: 15, pad: 5 };   // padded box: x [-23,17], z [-16,24], all y
function inNoGo(x, z) {
  return x >= NOGO.x - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && x <= NOGO.x + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad
      && z >= NOGO.z - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && z <= NOGO.z + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad;
}
```

Full-height column (not a y-slab): break-capable pathing under or over the
FEL base is foundation risk, not worth the shortcut.

**Layer 2 — position watchdog.** `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` take no coords
and a legal `#goto` can still PATH THROUGH the zone (baritone cannot be told
to route around it). So the log-tail position parser doubles as watchdog:
parsed position inside the padded box → immediately `msg #stop`, then
`msg #goto <camp waypoint>`, mark task `aborted:nogo` in `/status`, log loud.
Watchdog is the backstop; the gate is the front door. Drivers should also
prefer targets whose straight line to the bot doesn't cross the box.

## Upstream status 2026-09-01

Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform
in minecraft:blur/0" through "blur/5"; (2) hmc-specifics' JLine console
misbehaves when stdio is a plain pipe (no TTY), as the wrapper needs.

### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms

Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).

Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
release:
- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.

**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
redirection layer at all.
- hmc-specifics' console (`msg`, `connect`, `gui`, `click`) is confirmed to
  work identically with or without `-lwjgl` — see maintainer replies in
  [issue #230](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/230) and
  [issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390). Baritone
  chat-command control (part 3 of this doc) is unaffected by dropping the
  flag.
- Trade-off: a real (small, minimizable) game window per bot instance, and a
  sliver of real GPU/VRAM per client instead of zero. JVM heap budget in part
  6 is unaffected (that's CPU RAM, not GPU).
- If this stack ever moves to a true headless Linux box with no GPU at all,
  the Linux-native equivalent is Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe (software GL) in front
  of an un-patched launch — a working docker recipe is in
  [issue #249](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/249) (needs
  the `x11-xserver-utils` package per maintainer 3arthqu4ke, plus
  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Not directly usable on bare Windows (no X11);
  would need WSL2. Untested by this pass — field-verify separately if needed.
- If dropping `-lwjgl` is rejected and true headless is a hard requirement:
  this bucket is "fixable soon, not now" — file a new upstream issue with the
  exact blur/uniform log lines + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric. The
  maintainers (okafke, 3arthqu4ke) have a strong track record on this exact
  bug family — #388/#389 to merged fixes #406/#407 the same day.

### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)

Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").

Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
that way.

`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
  version of the above.

No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
reason to stand up a pty shim.

**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.

### Alternatives sanity check

- **Automatone** ([Ladysnake/Automatone](https://github.com/Ladysnake/Automatone),
  active, last updated 2026-07-10) — confirmed dead end for this stack, as
  suspected. It's a **server-side Fabric mod**: you attach Baritone pathing to
  any entity via a Java `EntityComponentFactory` registered server-side
  (`BaritoneAPI.getProvider().getBaritone(entity)`), driven entirely by
  in-process Java API calls. There is no protocol-level or console/chat
  control surface at all — mineflayer (an external protocol client) has
  nothing to hook into. Not usable, full stop.
- No other maintained "real headless Java client + baritone" project exists
  for 1.21.x besides HeadlessMc + hmc-specifics + official Baritone (PATH 1,
  already chosen). Official Baritone itself is healthy and current:
  [cabaletta/baritone releases](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases)
  show v1.16.0 (1.21.9/1.21.10), **v1.17.0 (1.21.11 — ours)**, v1.18.0 (26.1),
  v1.19.0 (26.2) — all four pushed 2026-08-31, one release per MC version,
  no drama.
- `Nevarielle/baritone-1.21.11` (community fork) still exists but is now
  redundant — official v1.17.0 covers 1.21.11 directly. Matches this doc's
  existing "obsolete — skip" call, no change needed.

### Verdict

- **Blocker 1 (render hang): fixable now, not via any HMC flag/release, but
  via a launch-config change — drop `-lwjgl`, run BariBrute's client with a
  real (minimized) window on the real GPU.** This sidesteps HeadlessMc's
  incomplete RenderPipeline/uniform emulation, the near-certain cause, which
  is not fixed or even filed upstream for the blur pipeline specifically
  (2.9.0/2.10.0 only fixed the neighboring memSlice-NPE and 26.2 DeviceLimits
  gaps). If a fully invisible process is a hard requirement, this drops to
  "fixable soon" — file upstream and wait; track record is good but nothing
  to point to yet.
- **Blocker 2 (JLine over plain pipe): fixable now** via config property, no
  pty wrapper needed — `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first, else the
  confirmed `hmc.jline.enabled=false` from issue #390. Keep never using
  `-commands` alongside hmc-specifics.
- **Alternatives: no change to PATH 1.** Automatone is confirmed unusable
  (server-side Java-API-only, no external-bot hook); official Baritone
  v1.17.0 for 1.21.11 remains current and healthy.

### Exact next actions

1. Drop `-lwjgl` from the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line in parts 2 and 4.
   Keep `-offline`. Add a small window size and OS-level minimize/off-screen
   placement in the wrapper's boot sequence in place of the render patch.
2. Add `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` to HMC's `config.properties` (or
   as a launch `-D` JVM arg). Only if console commands still misbehave over
   the wrapper's stdio pipe, switch to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` instead.
3. Do not add `-commands` anywhere — hmc-specifics alone is the console
   surface (maintainer guidance, issue #390).
4. If `-lwjgl` is ever required again (e.g. a true headless Linux box with no
   GPU), come back to this section and pursue Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe per the
   docker recipe in issue #249 — untested by this pass, field-verify
   separately.
5. Optional, only if committed to keeping true `-lwjgl` headless long-term:
   file a new issue on headlesshq/headlessmc with the exact blur/uniform log
   excerpt + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric, citing the memSlice/DeviceLimits
   precedent in this section to speed triage.
